standard_prerequisites.name: The defining relation of the Chern classes, obtained by expanding the cycle class of the zero scheme of a section of the tautological quotient
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, Definition \ref{definition-chern-classes} and the equation labelled equation-chern-classes, used at proof line 7200
standard_prerequisites.use: Specialized to the case of rank one, where $\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{L}) = X$ and $\mathcal{O}_{\mathbf{P}(\mathcal{L})}(1) = \mathcal{L}$, it reduces to $(-1)^1 c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap c_0 + (-1)^0 c_1 = 0$, which gives the claim.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Weil divisor associated to an invertible sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter chow.tex, Definition \ref{definition-divisor-invertible-sheaf} (invoked at proof line 7196)
standard_prerequisites.use: It supplies the construction that the proof denotes by $c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [X]$ and compares with the first Chern class.

core_obligations: Note that for an invertible sheaf the projective bundle is $X$ itself and the tautological quotient is $\mathcal{L}$, by the normalizations in force (proof lines 7197-7199).
Specialize the defining relation of the Chern classes to this rank one case, obtaining $(-1)^1 c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap c_0 + (-1)^0 c_1 = 0$ (proof lines 7200-7204).
Use $c_0 = [X]$ to identify $c_1$ with the divisor construction $c_1(\mathcal{L}) \cap [X]$ (proof lines 7205-7206).
proof_roadmap: Rank one normalizations of the projective bundle (proof lines 7197-7199).
The defining relation in rank one (proof lines 7200-7204).
Comparison with the divisor construction (proof lines 7205-7206).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the first Chern class of an invertible sheaf on an integral scheme of $\delta$-dimension $n$ with the Weil divisor associated to the sheaf, thereby connecting the two constructions (statement lines 7182-7192). The proof specializes the defining relation for Chern classes to rank one, where the projective bundle is the scheme itself and the tautological quotient is the given sheaf, and reads off the equality using $c_0 = [X]$. The specialization of the defining relation is the substance, so the claim is H2.
